THE BHARATIYA NYAYA  
SANHITA, 2023  
Chapter VI - XI  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY CHAPTER VI SECTION 100-146  
OF OFFENCES AFFECTING LIFE  
.
CULPABLE HOMICIDE (section 100):  




The word homicide is derived from two Latin words “Homo and Cido”.  
Homo means human and Cido means killing by a human.  
Homicide means killing of a human being by another human being.  
A homicide can be lawful or unlawful. Lawful homicide includes situations where  
a person who has caused the death of another cannot be blamed for his death.  
Culpable Homicide is in the category of unlawful homicide. The word Culpable  
means blame worthy. Thus, Culpable Homicide means killing of a human  
being by another human being in a blameworthy or criminal manner.  
As per this section Culpable Homicide means causing death intentionally, by  
intending to cause death or inflicting serious bodily injury likely to result in  
death, or knowingly engaging in an act with the awareness that it is likely to  
cause death, is considered the offense of culpable homicide.  
o Example: A lays sticks and turf over a pit, with the intention of thereby  
causing death, or with the knowledge that death is likely to be thereby  
caused. Z, believing the ground to be firm, treads on it, falls in and is killed.  
A has committed the offence of culpable homicide.  






If a person causes bodily injury to another who is already suffering from a disorder,  
disease, or bodily infirmity, and thereby speeds up the death of that person, it will  
be considered as causing death.  
If death is a result of bodily injury, the person causing such injury will be  
considered to have caused the death, even if proper remedies and skillful  
treatment could have prevented it.  
Causing the death of a child in the mother's womb is not considered homicide.  
However, causing the death of a living child, even if partially born and not yet fully  
breathed, may amount to culpable homicide.  
Section 101 deals with Culpable Homicide amounting to murder which states that  
culpable homicide is murder in certain situations. This makes us come to two  
conclusions:  
o For an act to be classified as murder it must first meet all the conditions of  
culpable homicide.  
o All acts of murder are culpable homicide, but all acts of culpable homicides  
are not murder.  
SECTION 101 STATES THAT CULPABLE HOMICIDE IS MURDER IN CERTAIN SITUATIONS  
 For an act to be classified as murder it must first meet all the conditions of culpable  
homicide.  
 All acts of murder are culpable homicide, but all acts of culpable homicides are not murder.  
2
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
.
MURDER (Section 101):  
Culpable homicide is considered murder, except in certain cases when:  

o The act causing death is done with the intention of causing death.  
o The act causing death is done with the intention of causing bodily injury  
known to likely cause death.  
o The act causing death is done with the intention of causing bodily injury,  
and the intended injury is sufficient to cause death in the ordinary course  
of nature.  
o The person committing the act knows it is so dangerous that it will probably  
cause death or serious bodily injury and commits the act without any  
excuse for taking such a risk.  
Example: A shoots Z with the intention of killing him. Z dies in  
consequence. A commits murder.  
Example: A intentionally gives Z a sword-cut or club-wound sufficient  
to cause the death of a man in the ordinary course of nature. Z dies  
in consequence. Here A is guilty of murder, although he may not have  
intended to cause Z’s death.  
.
CULPABLE HOMICIDE BY CAUSING DEATH OF PERSON OTHER THAN PERSON  
WHOSE DEATH WAS INTENDED (Section 102):  

If a person, while intending or knowing that their actions are likely to cause death,  
commits culpable homicide resulting in the death of a person they neither  
intended nor knew would likely die, the culpable homicide is of the same  
3
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
type as if they had caused the death of the person they intended or knew to  
be likely to die.  
KEY SECTIONS AND PENALTIES FOR INFLICTING HARM  
.
ORGANISED CRIME (Section 111):  

Any ongoing illegal activities such as kidnapping, robbery, vehicle theft,  
extortion, land grabbing, contract killing, economic offenses, cybercrimes, human  
trafficking, drug trafficking, weapon trafficking, or any illicit activities carried out by  
an individual or group, whether as part of an organized crime syndicate or on its  
behalf, using violence, threats, intimidation, coercion, or other unlawful means to  
gain material or financial benefits, are considered organized crime.  
If someone engages in organized crime:  

o If the offense leads to someone's death, they shall be punished with death  
penalty or life imprisonment, along with a fine of at least ten lakh  
rupees.  
o In any other case, they shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment  
between five years and life, coupled with a fine of at least five lakh  
rupees.  

Anyone aiding, attempting, conspiring, or knowingly assisting in the commission of  
organized crime, or engaging in any preparatory act, shall be punished with  
imprisonment ranging from five years to life, along with a fine of at least five  
lakh rupees.  
4
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  


A member of an organized crime syndicate shall be punished with imprisonment  
for a minimum of five years, extendable to life imprisonment, and a fine of at  
least five lakh rupees.  
Anyone deliberately hiding or sheltering a person involved in organized crime shall  
be sentenced to a minimum of three years in prison, extendable to life  
imprisonment, and fined at least five lakh rupees. However, this provision does  
not apply if the person providing shelter is the spouse of the offender.  
Possessing property obtained from organized crime or its proceeds shall be  
punished with imprisonment for a minimum of three years, up to life  
imprisonment, and a fine of at least two lakh rupees.  


If someone, on behalf of an organized crime syndicate member, possesses  
property without a satisfactory explanation, they shall be punished with  
imprisonment for a minimum of three years, extendable to ten years, and a  
fine of at least one lakh rupees.  
MEANING  
.
.
"Organized crime syndicate" refers to a group of two or more individuals, working together either  
independently or collectively as a gang, engaging in ongoing illegal activities.  
"Continuing unlawful activity" is when a person, either alone or as part of an organized crime  
group, commits a prohibited action punishable by imprisonment of three years or more. This  
includes economic offenses and applies when multiple charge sheets have been filed in the last  
ten years, and a court has recognized the offense.  
.
"Economic offense" encompasses crimes like criminal breach of trust, forgery, counterfeiting  
currency, engaging in hawala transactions, committing mass-marketing fraud, running fraudulent  
schemes, or any act with the intent to defraud banks, financial institutions, or other organizations  
.
PETTY ORGANISED CRIME (Section 112):  

Being part of a group or gang, if someone commits theft, snatching, cheating,  
unauthorized selling of tickets, unauthorized betting, gambling, selling public  
examination question papers, or similar criminal acts, it is considered petty  
organized crime.  

Committing any petty organized crime shall result in imprisonment for a  
minimum of one year, extendable to seven years, along with a fine.  
.
TERRORIST ACT (Section 113):  

Engaging in acts with the intent to threaten India's unity, integrity,  
sovereignty, security, or economic security, or to instill terror in people  
within India or abroad:  
o by engaging in acts, such as using explosives, firearms, or hazardous  
substances, with the intent to cause death, injury, property damage,  
5
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
disruption of essential services, harm to monetary stability, or destruction  
of defense-related properties in India or abroad.  
o by using criminal force or its display, attempting to do so, causing death, or  
attempting to cause death of any public functionary; or  
o by detaining, kidnapping, or abducting a person, threatening to harm or kill  
them, or performing any act to force the Government of India, any State  
Government, a foreign country's government, an international organization,  
or any person to perform or refrain from an act,  
shall constitute a terrorist act.  
MEANING  
.
.
"Public functionary" refers to constitutional authorities or any other functionary  
designated as such by the Central Government through an Official Gazette notification.  
"Counterfeit Indian currency" is currency declared as fake by an authorized forensic  
authority after examination, imitating or compromising key security features of Indian  
currency.  

Committing a terrorist act shall result in:  
o death penalty or life imprisonment, along with a fine if the act causes  
someone's death  
o imprisonment for a minimum of five years, extendable to life, and a fine in  
other cases.  


Conspiring, attempting, advocating, abetting, advising, or facilitating a terrorist act  
or any preparatory act shall be punishable with imprisonment for a minimum of  
five years, extendable to life, along with a fine.  
Organizing training camps for terrorist acts or recruiting individuals for such acts  
shall be punishable with imprisonment for a minimum of five years, which may  
extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.  
Being a member of an organization involved in terrorist acts shall be punished  
with imprisonment for life and fine.  


Harboring or concealing someone who committed a terrorist act shall be  
punishable with imprisonment for a minimum three-years, extendable to life,  
and fine.  
o Exception: This rule does not apply if the offender's spouse is involved in  
the concealment.  

Possessing property obtained from a terrorist act shall be punishable with  
imprisonment for life and fine.  
o The decision on whether to register the case under this section or the  
Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, will be made by an officer not  
below the rank of Superintendent of Police.  
6
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
OF HURT  
.
HURT (Section 114):  
Causing:  
o bodily pain,  

o disease, or  
o infirmity to a person  
is referred to as causing "hurt."  
.
.
VOLUNTARILY CAUSING HURT (Section 115):  

Causing harm to someone intentionally or with knowledge that it may occur  
is termed "voluntarily causing hurt."  

Anyone, other than in certain specified cases under section 122(1), who voluntarily  
causes hurt, shall be punished with imprisonment up to one year, a fine up to  
ten thousand rupees, or both.  
GRIEVOUS HURT (Section 116):  

The following types of severe harm are categorized as "grievous hurt":  
o Emasculation  
o Permanent loss of sight in either eye  
o Permanent loss of hearing in either ear  
o Loss of any limb or joint  
o Destruction or permanent impairment of any limb or joint  
o Permanent disfigurement of the head or face  
o Fracture or dislocation of a bone or tooth  
o Any injury that endangers life or causes severe bodily pain for fifteen days,  
making the person unable to pursue their regular activities.  
.
VOLUNTARILY CAUSING GRIEVOUS HURT (Section 117):  

Causing severe harm intentionally, knowing it might be grievous hurt, and  
actually causing grievous hurt is termed "voluntarily causing grievous hurt."  
Committing an offense as mentioned above and causing permanent disability or a  
persistent vegetative state resulting in hurt shall be punished with rigorous  
imprisonment for a minimum of ten years, extendable to life imprisonment,  
meaning imprisonment for the rest of the individual's natural life.  


To be considered as voluntarily causing grievous hurt, a person must both cause  
and intend or know that grievous hurt is likely. However, if the intention or  
knowledge is about causing one type of grievous hurt but the actual harm caused  
is of a different kind, it is still considered voluntarily causing grievous hurt.  
o Example: A, intending of knowing himself to be likely permanently to  
disfigure Z’s face, gives Z a blow which does not permanently disfigure Z’s  
7
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
face, but which causes Z to suffer severe bodily pain for the space of fifteen  
days. A has voluntarily caused grievous hurt.  


Causing grievous hurt voluntarily, except in cases specified in Section 122(2), shall  
be punished with imprisonment for up to seven years and a fine.  
When a group of five or more persons, working together, inflicts grievous hurt on  
an individual based on factors like race, caste, community, sex, place of birth,  
language, personal belief, or similar grounds, each member of the group is  
guilty of causing grievous hurt. The punishment includes imprisonment for  
up to seven years and a fine.  
.
VOLUNTARILY CAUSING HURT OR GRIEVOUS HURT BY DANGEROUS WEAPONS  
OR MEANS (Section 118):  

Causing hurt intentionally using instruments like weapons, fire, poison,  
explosives, or harmful substances shall be punished with imprisonment up to  
three years, a fine up to twenty thousand rupees, or both, except in cases  
specified in Section 122(1).  

Causing grievous hurt intentionally using any means as mentioned above,  
except in cases specified in Section 122(2), shall be punished. The penalty shall  
include imprisonment for life or imprisonment ranging from one year to ten  
years, along with a fine.  
.
.
.
VOLUNTARILY CAUSING HURT OR GRIEVOUS HURT TO EXTORT PROPERTY, OR  
TO CONSTRAIN TO AN ILLEGAL ACT (Section 119):  

Causing hurt intentionally to extort property or valuable security or to compel the  
victim or related persons to engage in illegal activities shall be punished with  
imprisonment for up to ten years, along with a fine.  

Causing grievous hurt intentionally for any purpose specified above shall be  
punished with imprisonment for life or imprisonment for a term up to ten  
years, along with a fine.  
VOLUNTARILY CAUSING HURT OR GRIEVOUS HURT TO EXTORT CONFESSION,  
OR TO COMPEL RESTORATION OF PROPERTY (Section 120):  

If someone intentionally hurts another person to force them or someone related to  
them to confess, provide information, return property, settle a claim, or reveal  
details that could help detect a crime, they shall be punished with imprisonment  
for up to seven years and fined.  
o A, a police officer, tortures Z in order to induce Z to confess that he  
committed a crime. A is guilty of an offence under this section.  
VOLUNTARILY CAUSING HURT OR GRIEVOUS HURT TO DETER PUBLIC SERVANT  
FROM HIS DUTY (section 121):  

If someone voluntarily causes hurts a public servant while they are doing their job,  
or with the intent to stop them from doing their duty, they shall be punished with  
imprisonment up to five years or with fine, or both.  
8
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  

If someone voluntarily causes serious hurt to a public servant while they are doing  
their job, or with the intent to stop them from doing their duty, they shall be  
punishable with imprisonment for at least one year, up to a maximum of ten  
years, and shall also be liable to fine.  
.
VOLUNTARILY CAUSING HURT OR GRIEVOUS HURT ON PROVOCATION (Section  
122):  

If someone hurts another person in response to serious and immediate  
provocation, and they did not mean to harm anyone else, they shall be punished  
with imprisonment up to one month or with fine of up to five thousand  
rupees, or with both.  

If someone causes serious harm to another person in response to intense and  
immediate provocation, and they did not mean to harm anyone else seriously, they  
shall be punished with imprisonment up to five years or with fine of up to ten  
thousand rupees, or with both.  
.
.
CAUSING HURT BY MEANS OF POISON, ETC., WITH INTENT TO COMMIT AN  
OFFENCE (Section 123):  

If someone gives another person poison or any harmful substance intending to  
cause harm, commit a crime, or knowing it could cause harm, they shall be  
punished with imprisonment for up to ten years and shall also be liable to  
fine.  
VOLUNTARILY CAUSING GRIEVOUS HURT BY USE OF ACID, ETC. (Section 124):  

Causing severe harm, deformity, or disability to someone by throwing acid or using  
any means with the intent to cause such injury shall be punishable with  
imprisonment for a minimum of ten years extendable up to life and with fine.  
Fine, meant to cover medical expenses, will be imposed and paid to the victim.  
If someone tries to throw acid on another person or use any means to cause  
permanent harm or severe injuries, they shall be sentenced to imprisonment for  
a minimum of five years extendable up to seven years, and shall also be  
liable to fine.  

o Permanent or partial damage or deformity or permanent vegetative state  
shall not be required to be irreversible.  
MEANING  
.
"Acid" includes any substance which has acidic or corrosive character or burning nature,  
that is capable of causing bodily injury leading to scars or disfigurement or temporary or  
permanent disability.  
9
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
.
ACT ENDANGERING LIFE OR PERSONAL SAFETY OF OTHERS (Section 125)  

If someone endangers others recklessly, they shall be punished with  
imprisonment of three months, or with fine which may extend to two  
thousand five hundred rupees, or with both.  
o If their actions cause harm, the penalty shall extend to six months  
imprisonment, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or  
with both.  
o If severe harm occurs, the punishment shall be imprisonment up to three  
years or with fine of up to ten thousand rupees, or with both.  
OF WRONGFUL RESTRAINT AND WRONGFUL CONFINEMENT  
. WRONGFUL RESTRAINT (Section 126):  

If someone deliberately blocks another person's path, stopping them from  
going where they have the right to go, it's considered wrongful restraint.  
o However, the obstruction of a private way over land or water which a person  
in good faith believes himself to have a lawful right to obstruct, is not an  
offence under this rule.  
o Example: A obstructs a path along which Z has a right to pass, A not  
believing in good faith that he has a right to stop the path. Z is thereby  
prevented from passing. A wrongfully restrains Z.  

Punishment: simple imprisonment for up to one month or with fine which may  
extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.  
.
WRONGFUL CONFINEMENT (Section 127):  

If someone unlawfully stops another person from going beyond certain  
limits, it is called "wrongfully confining" that person.  
o Example: A causes Z to go within a walled space, and locks Z in. Z is thus  
prevented from proceeding in any direction beyond the circumscribing line  
of wall. A wrongfully confines Z.  


Punishment: imprisonment for up to one year or with fine of up to five thousand  
rupees, or with both.  
If someone unlawfully restricts another person for three days or more, they shall  
be punished with imprisonment for up to three years or with fine of up to ten  
thousand rupees, or with both.  


If someone unlawfully restricts another person for ten days or more, they shall be  
sentenced to imprisonment for up to five years and fined a minimum of ten  
thousand rupees.  
If someone unlawfully keeps a person confined, knowing that a Court order for  
their release has been issued, they shall be punished with imprisonment for  
up to two years, in addition to any other punishment they may receive under  
this chapter, and shall also be fined.  
10  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  



If someone unlawfully confines a person with the intention to keep it secret from  
anyone concerned or authorities, they shall be sentenced to imprisonment  
for up to three years, in addition to any other punishment for wrongful  
confinement, and shall also be liable to fine.  
If someone unlawfully confines a person to force them or someone connected  
to them to give up property, valuable items, or do something illegal, they shall  
be sentenced to imprisonment for up to three years and shall also be liable  
to fine.  
If someone unlawfully confines a person for the purpose of extorting from them  
or someone related to them to confess, provide information, return property,  
settle a claim, or give information for the detection of an offense, they shall be  
sentenced to imprisonment for up to three years and shall also be liable to  
fined.  
OF CRIMINAL FORCE AND ASSAULT  
.
FORCE (Section 128):  
A person is considered to use force against another if they make that person  

move, change their motion, or stop moving. This also applies if they cause  
any substance to move or change in a way that brings it into contact with the  
other person's body or anything they are wearing, or with anything so  
situated that such contact affects that other’s sense of feeling.  
o The force can be applied by:  
the person's own physical effort,  
arranging a substance to cause motion without further action, or  
influencing an animal to move or change its motion.  
.
CRIMINAL FORCE (Section 129):  

If someone deliberately applies force to another person without their  
agreement, with the intention of committing an offense or causing harm,  
fear, or annoyance, it is considered criminal force.  
o Example: Z is riding in a palanquin. A, intending to rob Z, seizes the pole  
and stops the palanquin. Here A has caused cessation of motion to Z, and  
he has done this by his own bodily power. A has therefore used force to Z;  
and as A has acted thus intentionally, without Z’s consent, in order to the  
commission of an offence. A has used criminal force to Z.  
.
ASSAULT (Section 130):  

If someone makes a gesture or prepares in a way that they know might make  
others think they are about to use criminal force, it's considered an assault.  

Mere words do not amount to an assault, but the combination of words and  
actions can turn gestures or preparations into an assault.  
11  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
o Example: A shakes his fist at Z, intending or knowing it to be likely that he  
may thereby cause Z to believe that A is about to strike Z. A has committed  
an assault.  
.
PUNISHMENT FOR ASSAULT OR CRIMINAL FORCE OTHERWISE THAN ON GRAVE  
PROVOCATION (Section 131):  

If someone assaults or uses criminal force against another person without that  
person giving a serious and immediate reason, they shall be punished with  
imprisonment for up to three months or with fine of up to one thousand  
rupees, or with both.  


If the provocation is intentionally sought or provoked by the offender, or if it  
arises from legal actions, the punishment shall not be reduced.  
Whether the provocation is significant enough to lessen the offense is determined  
as a matter of fact.  
.
.
ASSAULT OR CRIMINAL FORCE TO DETER PUBLIC SERVANT FROM DISCHARGE  
OF HIS DUTY (Section 132):  

If someone assaults or uses criminal force against a public servant while they are  
doing their job, or with the intent to stop them from discharging their duty, they shall  
be sentenced to imprisonment for up to two years or with fine, or with both.  
ASSAULT OR CRIMINAL FORCE WITH INTENT TO DISHONOUR PERSON,  
OTHERWISE THAN ON GRAVE PROVOCATION (Section 133):  

If someone assaults or uses criminal force against another person with the  
intention of dishonoring them, without a serious and immediate provocation from  
that person, they shall be punished with imprisonment for up to two years or  
with fine or with both.  
.
.
ASSAULT OR CRIMINAL FORCE IN ATTEMPT TO COMMIT THEFT OF PROPERTY  
CARRIED BY A PERSON (Section 134):  

If someone assaults or uses criminal force against another person while attempting  
to steal something they are wearing or carrying, they shall be punished with  
imprisonment for up to two years or with fine, or with both.  
ASSAULT OR CRIMINAL FORCE IN ATTEMPT TO WRONGFULLY CONFINE A  
PERSON (Section 135):  

If someone assaults or uses criminal force while trying to unlawfully confine  
another person, they shall be sentenced to imprisonment for up to one year or  
with fine up to five thousand rupees, or with both.  
.
ASSAULT OR CRIMINAL FORCE ON GRAVE PROVOCATION (Section 136):  
12  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  

If someone assaults or uses criminal force against another person due to serious  
and immediate provocation from that person, they shall be punished with simple  
imprisonment for up to one month or with fine up to one thousand rupees,  
or with both.  
OF KIDNAPPING, ABDUCTION, SLAVERY AND FORCED LABOUR  
.
KIDNAPPING (Section 137):  

Kidnapping is of two types:  
o kidnapping from India occurs when someone takes a person beyond India's  
borders without their or their authorized guardian's consent and  
o kidnapping from lawful guardianship involves taking a child or a person with  
unsound mind away from their lawful guardian without consent.  
The term "lawful guardian" includes anyone legally entrusted with their care.  
There is an exception for a person acting in good faith believing they are the  
father of an illegitimate child or entitled to lawful custody, unless the act is for an  
immoral or unlawful purpose.  



Whoever kidnaps someone shall be punished with imprisonment for up to  
seven years and shall also be liable to fine.  
.
.
ABDUCTION (Section 138):  
If someone uses force or deceitful methods to make a person leave a place,  
it is called abduction.  

KIDNAPPING OR MAIMING A CHILD FOR PURPOSES OF BEGGING (Section 139):  

If anyone kidnaps a child or, without being the lawful guardian, takes custody of  
the child with the intention of using them for begging, they shall be punished with  
rigorous imprisonment for at least ten years, up to life imprisonment, and  
shall also be liable to fine.  



Anyone causing severe harm to a child for the purpose of using them for begging  
shall be imprisoned for a minimum of twenty years, up to life imprisonment,  
along with a fine.  
If a person, not the lawful guardian, employs or uses a child for begging, it is  
presumed, unless proven otherwise, that they kidnapped or obtained custody  
of the child for begging purposes.  
"Begging" means:  
o asking for or receiving alms in public by pretending to sing, dance, tell  
fortunes, perform tricks, sell items, or in any other way;  
o going onto private property to ask for or receive alms;  
o displaying or showing, with the intention of getting alms, any sore, wound,  
injury, deformity, or disease, whether it's on oneself, another person, or an  
animal;  
13  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
o using a child as an exhibit with the aim of asking for or receiving alms.  
.
KIDNAPPING OR ABDUCTING IN ORDER TO MURDER OR FOR RANSOM, ETC.  
(Section 140):  

If someone kidnaps a person with the intention of murdering them or putting them  
in danger of being murdered, they shall be sentenced to life imprisonment or  
rigorous imprisonment for up to ten years, along with fine.  
o Example: A kidnaps Z from India, intending or knowing it to be likely that Z  
may be sacrificed to an idol. A has committed the offence defined in this  
section.  

If someone kidnaps a person, keeps them in detention, and threatens to cause  
harm or actually causes harm to compel the government, foreign state,  
organization, or another person to do something or pay a ransom, they shall be  
punished with death or life imprisonment, along with a fine.  
If someone kidnaps a person with the intention of secretly and wrongfully confining  
them, they shall be punished with imprisonment for up to seven years and  
shall also be liable to fine.  


If someone kidnaps a person with the intention of causing them grievous harm,  
slavery, or subjecting them to unnatural acts or puts them in danger of such  
treatment, they shall be punished with imprisonment for up to ten years and  
shall also be liable to fine.  
.
.
IMPORTATION OF GIRL OR BOY FROM FOREIGN COUNTRY (Section 141):  

If someone brings a girl under 21 years or a boy under 18 years into India from  
another country, intending or knowing that they will likely be forced or seduced into  
illicit intercourse with someone, they shall be punished with imprisonment for  
up to ten years and shall also be liable to fine.  
TRAFFICKING OF PERSON (Section 142):  

Engaging in trafficking involves recruiting, transporting, harboring, transferring,  
or receiving a person for exploitation. This can be done through threats, force,  
coercion, abduction, fraud, abuse of power, or inducement, including the exchange  
of payments or benefits to gain the consent of someone in control of the person  
being trafficked.  
o “Exploitation” shall include any act of physical exploitation or any form  
of sexual exploitation, slavery or practices similar to slavery, servitude,  
beggary or forced removal of organs.  
o The consent of the victim is immaterial in determination of the offence of  
trafficking.  

Punishment: Rigorous imprisonment for a minimum of seven years, up to ten  
years, and shall also be liable to fine.  
14  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
o Offence involves the trafficking of more than one person, it shall be  
punishable with rigorous for a minimum of ten years, up to life  
imprisonment, and shall also be liable to fine.  
o Offence involves the trafficking of a child, it shall be punishable with  
rigorous imprisonment for a minimum of ten years, up to imprisonment for  
life, and shall also be liable to fine.  
o Offence involves the trafficking of more than one child, it shall be  
punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a minimum of fourteen years, up  
to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.  
o A person is convicted of trafficking a child multiple times, they shall be  
sentenced to life imprisonment, meaning imprisonment for the rest of their  
natural life, and shall also be liable to fine.  
o A public servant or police officer is involved in human trafficking, they  
shall be punished with life imprisonment, meaning imprisonment for the rest  
of their natural life, and shall also be liable to fine.  
.
EXPLOITATION OF A TRAFFICKED PERSON (Section 144):  

If someone exploits a trafficked child for sexual purposes, they shall be  
imprisoned for a minimum of five years, up to ten years, and shall also be  
fined.  

Similarly, engaging in sexual exploitation of a trafficked person shall lead to  
imprisonment for a minimum of three years, up to seven years, along with  
fine.  
.
.
HABITUAL DEALING IN SLAVES (Section 145):  

Engaging in the habitual import, export, removal, purchase, sale, trafficking, or  
dealing in slaves shall be punishable by either life imprisonment or  
imprisonment for a term up to ten years, along with a fine.  
UNLAWFUL COMPULSORY LABOUR (Section 146):  

Forcing someone to work against their will shall be punishable with imprisonment  
for up to one yea or with fine, or with both.  
OF OFFENCES AGAINST THE STATE CHAPTER VII SECTION 147-158  
.
The main object of including this chapter is to punish each and every individual who  
tries to create some kind of discord or disharmony between the Government and  
the people. In a democratic country it will be very harmful to the interests of the people at  
large if any person(s) wages war against the State and disrupts peace. The chapter also  
punishes certain offences like “sedition” which are termed serious offences against the  
state.  
15  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
.
.
IN THIS CHAPTER SEDITION HAS BEEN REMOVED AS AN OFFENCE.  
Instead, there is a new offence for acts endangering India's sovereignty, unity  
and integrity.  
.
WAGING, OR ATTEMPTING TO WAGE WAR, OR ABETTING WAGING OF WAR,  
AGAINST GOVERNMENT OF INDIA (Section 147):  

Engaging in or attempting to wage war against the Government of India, or  
supporting such actions, shall be punishable with death or life imprisonment,  
and shall also be liable for fine.  
o Example: A joins an insurrection against the Government of India. A has  
committed the offence defined in this section.  
.
CONSPIRACY TO COMMIT OFFENCES PUNISHABLE BY SECTION 147 (Section  
148):  

Anyone conspiring to commit offenses punishable under Section 147, or conspiring  
to overawe the Central Government or any State Government using criminal force,  
shall be liable to imprisonment for life or up to ten years, along with a fine.  
The actual commission of an illegal act is not necessary for a conspiracy under  
this section.  

.
COLLECTING ARMS, ETC., WITH INTENTION OF WAGING WAR AGAINST  
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA (Section 149):  

Anyone gathering men, arms, or ammunition or preparing to wage war with the  
intention of waging or being prepared to wage war against the Government of India  
shall be punished with either life imprisonment or imprisonment for up to ten  
years, and shall also be liable to fine.  
.
.
CONCEALING WITH INTENT TO FACILITATE DESIGN TO WAGE WAR (Section 150):  

Anyone who hides the existence of a plan to wage war against the Government of  
India, intending to facilitate or knowing it will likely facilitate such war, can be  
punished with imprisonment for a term up to ten years and fined.  
ASSAULTING PRESIDENT, GOVERNOR, ETC., WITH INTENT TO COMPEL OR  
RESTRAIN EXERCISE OF ANY LAWFUL POWER (Section 151):  

Anyone intending to influence or force the President of India or Governor of any  
State to exercise or refrain from exercising their lawful powers, through assault,  
wrongful restraint, or intimidation using criminal force, shall be punished with  
imprisonment for up to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.  
16  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
.
ACT ENDANGERING SOVEREIGNTY, UNITY AND INTEGRITY OF INDIA (Section  
152):  

Anyone purposefully or knowingly using words, signs, visible representation,  
electronic communication, financial means, or any other method to incite  
secession, armed rebellion, subversive activities, or encourage separatist feelings  
that endanger India's sovereignty, unity, and integrity shall be punished with  
life imprisonment or imprisonment up to seven years, along with a fine.  
Expressing disapproval of Government measures by lawful means, without  
attempting the activities mentioned in this section, does not constitute an  
offense under this section.  

.
.
WAGING WAR AGAINST GOVERNMENT OF ANY FOREIGN STATE AT PEACE WITH  
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA (Section 153):  

Engaging in or attempting to wage war against a foreign State at peace with the  
Government of India, or aiding such actions, shall be punished with  
imprisonment for life, to which fine may be added, or with imprisonment up  
to seven years, to which fine may be added, or with fine.  
COMMITTING DEPREDATION ON TERRITORIES OF FOREIGN STATE AT PEACE  
WITH GOVERNMENT OF INDIA (Section 154):  

Anyone who commits depredation or prepares to commit depredation on the  
territories of a foreign State at peace with the Government of India shall be  
punished with imprisonment for up to seven years and shall also be liable to  
fine, and forfeiture of any property used or intended for such actions.  
.
.
RECEIVING PROPERTY TAKEN BY WAR OR DEPREDATION MENTIONED IN  
SECTIONS 153 AND 154 (Section 155):  

Receiving property, knowing it was taken during the commission of offenses under  
sections 153 and 154, shall be punishable with imprisonment for up to seven  
years, along with a fine and forfeiture of the received property.  
PUBLIC SERVANT VOLUNTARILY ALLOWING PRISONER OF STATE OR WAR TO  
ESCAPE (Section 156):  

A public servant, entrusted with the custody of a State prisoner or prisoner of war,  
who willingly allows the prisoner to escape from confinement, shall be liable to  
punishment with life imprisonment or imprisonment up to ten years, and  
shall also be liable to fine.  
.
PUBLIC SERVANT NEGLIGENTLY SUFFERING SUCH PRISONER TO ESCAPE  
(Section 157):  
17  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  

A public servant, responsible for the custody of a State prisoner or prisoner of war,  
who negligently allows such prisoner to escape from confinement, shall be  
punished with simple imprisonment for up to three years, along with a fine.  
.
AIDING ESCAPE OF, RESCUING OR HARBOURING SUCH PRISONER (Section 158):  

Anyone who knowingly helps a State prisoner or prisoner of war escape from lawful  
custody, rescues or attempts to rescue such a prisoner, harbors or conceals an  
escaped prisoner, or resists their recapture shall be liable to punishment with  
life imprisonment or imprisonment up to ten years, along with fine.  
If a State prisoner or prisoner of war, who is allowed to be outside custody  
on parole within specific limits in India, goes beyond those allowed limits, it  
is considered an escape from lawful custody.  

OF OFFENCES RELATING TO THE ARMY, NAVY AND AIR FORCE CHAPTER VIII SECTION  
159-168  
.
This Chapter deals with offences committed by civilians in relation to officers in Army,  
Navy and Airforce of the Government of India. The main objective of this chapter is to  
maintain discipline and order in the Armed Forces of the Union.  
.
ABETTING MUTINY, OR ATTEMPTING TO SEDUCE A SOLDIER, SAILOR OR  
AIRMAN FROM HIS DUTY (Section 159):  

If anyone encourages an officer, soldier, sailor, or airman in the Indian Army, Navy,  
or Air Force to commit mutiny or tries to lead them away from their loyalty or duty,  
they shall be punished with imprisonment for life or imprisonment for up to  
ten years, along with a fine.  
.
ABETMENT OF MUTINY, IF MUTINY IS COMMITTED IN CONSEQUENCE THEREOF  
(Section 160):  

If someone supports or encourages an officer, soldier, sailor, or airman in the  
Indian Army, Navy, or Air Force to commit mutiny, and if mutiny occurs as a result  
of that encouragement, they shall be punished with death or with life  
imprisonment, or imprisonment for up to ten years, along with a fine.  
.
ABETMENT OF ASSAULT BY SOLDIER, SAILOR OR AIRMAN ON HIS SUPERIOR  
OFFICER, WHEN IN EXECUTION OF HIS OFFICE (Section 161):  

If someone encourages or supports an assault by an officer, soldier, sailor, or  
airman in the Indian Army, Navy, or Air Force on a superior officer while the  
superior officer is performing his duties, they shall be punished with  
imprisonment for up to three years and shall also be liable to fine.  
18  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
.
ABETMENT OF SUCH ASSAULT, IF ASSAULT COMMITTED (Section 162):  

If someone encourages or supports an assault by an officer, soldier, sailor, or  
airman in the Indian Army, Navy, or Air Force on a superior officer while the  
superior officer is performing his duties, and if the assault happens as a result of  
that encouragement, they shall be punished with imprisonment for up to seven  
years and shall also be liable to fine.  
.
.
ABETMENT OF DESERTION OF SOLDIER, SAILOR OR AIRMAN (Section 163):  

If someone encourages or supports the desertion of any officer, soldier, sailor, or  
airman in the Indian Army, Navy, or Air Force, they shall be punished with  
imprisonment for up to two years, or with a fine, or with both.  
HARBOURING DESERTER (Section 164):  

If someone knowingly harbors an officer, soldier, sailor, or airman who has  
deserted from the Indian Army, Navy, or Air Force, they shall be punished with  
imprisonment for up to two years or with fine, or with both.  
However, this provision does not apply when the deserter is harbored by their  
spouse.  

.
DESERTER  
CONCEALED  
ON  
BOARD  
MERCHANT  
VESSEL  
THROUGH  
NEGLIGENCE OF MASTER (Section 165):  

If a deserter from the Indian Army, Navy, or Air Force is concealed on board a  
merchant vessel, the master or person in charge shall be liable to a penalty, not  
exceeding three thousand rupees, if they could have known about the  
concealment but for negligence or lack of discipline on the vessel.  
.
ABETMENT OF ACT OF INSUBORDINATION BY SOLDIER, SAILOR OR AIRMAN  
(Section 166):  

If someone encourages and knows that they are supporting an act of  
insubordination by an officer, soldier, sailor, or airman in the Indian Army, Navy, or  
Air Force, and if the insubordination occurs as a result, they shall be punished  
with imprisonment for up to two years or with fine, or with both.  
.
.
PERSONS SUBJECT TO CERTAIN ACTS (Section 167):  

Persons subject to the Air Force Act, 1950, the Army Act, 1950, and the Navy Act,  
1957, shall not liable to be punished under the BNS for offenses defined in  
this Chapter.  
WEARING GARB OR CARRYING TOKEN USED BY SOLDIER, SAILOR OR AIRMAN  
(Section 168):  

Anyone who, not being a soldier, sailor, or airman in the service of the Government  
of India, wears a uniform or carries any item resembling those used by such  
19  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
personnel with the intent to deceive others into believing that he is part of the  
military, shall be punished with imprisonment for up to three months, or with  
fine of up to two thousand rupees, or with both.  
OF OFFENCES RELATING TO ELECTIONS CHAPTER IX SECTION 169-177  
.
The objective of this Chapter is to provide for the punishment for malpractices in  
connection with elections and attempts to safeguard the purity of system of elections in  
India.  
.
CANDIDATE, ELECTORAL RIGHT DEFINED (Section 169):  

In this Chapter:  
o "Candidate" refers to a person nominated for any election.  
o "Electoral right" encompasses the right of an individual to become or  
cease to be a candidate, or to participate or abstain from voting in an  
election.  
.
BRIBERY (Section 170):  

Giving a gratification to influence someone's electoral right or as a reward  
for exercising such a right, or accepting a gratification for oneself or another  
person for the same purpose, constitutes bribery.  
o Declarations of public policy or promises of public action are exempt from  
this offense.  


Offering, agreeing to give, or attempting to procure a gratification is treated  
as giving a gratification.  
Obtaining, agreeing to accept, or attempting to obtain a gratification is  
considered accepting a gratification. Accepting a gratification as a motive for  
doing something one does not intend to do or as a reward for actions falls  
under bribery.  
.
UNDUE INFLUENCE AT ELECTIONS (Section 171):  



Anyone who voluntarily interferes or attempts to interfere with the free  
exercise of any electoral right commits the offense of undue influence at an  
election.  
Anyone who threatens a candidate or voter with injury or induces a candidate  
or voter to believe they will incur divine displeasure or spiritual censure  
interferes with the free exercise of the electoral right.  
Declarations of public policy, promises of public action, or the mere exercise  
of a legal right without intent to interfere with an electoral right are not deemed  
to be interference under this section.  
.
PERSONATION AT ELECTIONS (Section 172):  
20  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  

If someone, during an election, applies for a voting paper using the name of  
another person (living or dead) or a fake name, or if they have already voted  
and try to vote again in their own name, it is considered the offense of  
personation at an election.  

This does not apply if a person is authorized to vote as a proxy for someone else  
according to the existing laws.  
.
.
PUNISHMENT FOR BRIBERY (Section 173):  

If someone commits the offense of bribery, they shall be punished with  
imprisonment for up to one year, or with a fine, or with both.  
If bribery involves treating, it will be punished with a fine only.  
o Treating refers to bribery where the gratification involves providing food,  
drink, entertainment, or provision.  

PUNISHMENT FOR UNDUE INFLUENCE OR PERSONATION AT AN ELECTION  
(Section 174):  

If someone commits the offense of undue influence or personation at an election,  
they shall be punished with imprisonment for up to one year, or with a fine,  
or with both.  
.
.
FALSE STATEMENT IN CONNECTION WITH AN ELECTION (Section 175):  

If someone intentionally makes or publishes a false statement about the personal  
character or conduct of a candidate to influence the election result, they shall be  
punished with a fine.  
ILLEGAL PAYMENTS IN CONNECTION WITH AN ELECTION (Section 176):  

If someone spends money on behalf of a candidate for election without the  
candidate's written authority, they shall be fined up to ten thousand rupees.  
If the person gets written approval from the candidate within ten days for  
expenses not exceeding ten rupees, it will be considered authorized.  

.
FAILURE TO KEEP ELECTION ACCOUNTS (Section 177):  

If someone, as required by law, fails to keep accounts of expenses related to an  
election, they shall be fined up to five thousand rupees.  
OF OFFENCES RELATING TO COIN, CURRENCY-NOTES, BANK-NOTES, AND  
GOVERNMENT STAMPS CHAPTER X SECTION 178-188  
.
COUNTERFEITING COIN, GOVERNMENT STAMPS, CURRENCY-NOTES OR BANK-  
NOTES (Section 178):  
21  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  

Anyone who counterfeits or knowingly engages in the process of counterfeiting  
coins, revenue stamps, currency notes, or banknotes shall be punished with  
imprisonment for life or up to ten years, along with a fine.  
MEANING  
.
"Bank Note" means a promissory note or engagement for the payment of money to the bearer  
on demand. It is issued by a person engaged in banking anywhere globally or by or under the  
authority of a State or Sovereign Power. The purpose is for it to be used as equivalent to or as a  
substitute for money.  
.
.
.
.
“Coin” means any metal used as money, stamped, and issued by or under the authority of any  
State or Sovereign Power, as defined in the Coinage Act, 2011.  
Counterfeiting a government stamp involves making a genuine stamp of one denomination  
appear like a genuine stamp of a different denomination.  
A person commits Counterfeiting of coin when the person, with the intent to deceive or  
knowing that deception is likely, makes a genuine coin appear like a different coin.  
The offense of "counterfeiting coin" also covers reducing the weight, changing the  
composition, or altering the appearance of the coin.  
.
USING AS GENUINE, FORGED OR COUNTERFEIT COIN, GOVERNMENT STAMP,  
CURRENCY-NOTES OR BANK-NOTES (Section 179):  

Anyone who knowingly imports, exports, sells, delivers, buys, receives, traffics, or  
uses as genuine any forged or counterfeit coin, stamp, currency-note, or bank-note  
shall be punished with imprisonment for life or imprisonment for a term up  
to ten years, along with a fine.  
.
POSSESSION OF FORGED OR COUNTERFEIT COIN, GOVERNMENT STAMP,  
CURRENCY-NOTES OR BANK-NOTES (Section 180):  

Anyone found in possession of a forged or counterfeit coin, stamp, currency-note,  
or bank-note, knowing or believing it to be fake and with the intent to use it as  
genuine, shall be punished with imprisonment for up to seven years or with  
fine, or with both.  

If the person can prove the lawful source of possession, it will not be  
considered an offense under this section.  
.
MAKING OR POSSESSING INSTRUMENTS OR MATERIALS FOR FORGING OR  
COUNTERFEITING COIN, GOVERNMENT STAMP, CURRENCY-NOTES OR BANK-  
NOTES (Section 181):  
22  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  

Anyone involved in making, mending, buying, selling, or possessing machinery,  
die, instrument, or material with the intent to forge or counterfeit coins, government  
revenue stamps, currency-notes, or bank-notes shall be punished with  
imprisonment for life or up to ten years, along with a fine.  
.
MAKING OR USING DOCUMENTS RESEMBLING CURRENCY-NOTES OR BANK-  
NOTES (Section 182):  



Anyone creating, causing to be made, or using a document that looks like a  
currency-note or bank-note, or is so similar that it could deceive, may be subject  
to a fine of up to three hundred rupees.  
If someone, whose name is on an illegal document, refuses to tell the police officer  
the name and address of the person who made it, they shall be fined up to six  
hundred rupees.  
If a person is charged with an offence related to a document, and someone's name  
is on that document or on another document connected to it, it is presumed,  
unless proven otherwise, that the person caused the document to be made.  
.
EFFACING WRITING FROM SUBSTANCE BEARING GOVERNMENT STAMP, OR  
REMOVING FROM DOCUMENT A STAMP USED FOR IT, WITH INTENT TO CAUSE  
LOSS TO GOVERNMENT (Section 183):  

If someone intentionally removes or erases any writing or document from a  
substance that carries a government-issued revenue stamp, or takes off a stamp  
used for a document to use it on another, with the fraudulent intent to cause a loss  
to the government, they shall be punished with imprisonment for up to three  
years, or with a fine, or with both.  
.
USING GOVERNMENT STAMP KNOWN TO HAVE BEEN BEFORE USED (Section  
184):  

If someone knowingly and with the intent to cause a loss to the government uses  
a stamp issued by the government for revenue purposes, which has been used  
before, they shall be punished with imprisonment for up to two years, or with  
a fine, or with both.  
.
.
ERASURE OF MARK DENOTING THAT STAMP HAS BEEN USED (Section 185):  

If someone fraudulently erases or removes a mark on a government-issued  
revenue stamp indicating its use, with the intent to cause a loss to the government,  
or knowingly possesses, sells, or disposes of such a stamp, they shall be  
punished with imprisonment for up to three years, or with fine, or with both.  
PROHIBITION OF FICTITIOUS STAMPS (Section 186):  

Anyone who makes, knowingly uses, deals in, sells, or possesses a fictitious stamp  
for postal purposes, or possesses any die, plate, instrument, or materials for  
23  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
making fictitious stamps without lawful excuse, shall be punished with a fine of  
up to two hundred rupees.  


Any stamp, die, plate, instrument, or materials for making fictitious stamps found  
in possession of a person may be seized and, upon seizure, shall be forfeited.  
"Fictitious stamp" refers to any stamp falsely claiming to be issued by the  
Government for denoting a postage rate, or any imitation or representation of such  
a stamp.  

In this section and the related sections (Section 178 to 181 and 183 to 185), when  
the term "Government" when used in connection with, or in reference to any stamp  
issued for the purpose of denoting a rate of postage, shall be deemed to include  
the person or persons authorized by law to administer executive  
Government in any part of India or in any foreign country.  
.
.
PERSON EMPLOYED IN MINT CAUSING COIN TO BE OF DIFFERENT WEIGHT OR  
COMPOSITION FROM THAT FIXED BY LAW (Section 187):  

Any person employed in a legally established mint in India who intentionally takes  
action or neglects duties to alter the weight or composition of a coin issued from  
that mint, deviating from the legal standards, shall be punished with  
imprisonment for up to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.  
UNLAWFULLY TAKING COINING INSTRUMENT FROM MINT (Section 188):  

Anyone who, without lawful authority, removes any coining tool or instrument from  
a legally established mint in India shall be punished with imprisonment for a  
term up to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.  
OF OFFENCES AGAINST THE PUBLIC TRANQUILLITY CHAPTER XI SECTION 189-197  
UNLAWFUL ASSEMBLY (Section 189):  
.

A gathering of five or more people becomes an "unlawful assembly" if they  
share a common purpose, such as:  
o using criminal force to overawe the Central Government, State  
Government, Parliament, Legislature, or a public servant.  
o resisting the execution of any law or legal process.  
o committing mischief, criminal trespass, or other offenses.  
o using criminal force to take possession of property, deprive someone of  
their rights, or enforce a supposed right.  
o using criminal force to compel someone to do something they are not  
legally bound to do or to refrain from a legal action.  
An assembly that was initially lawful can later become unlawful.  

If someone:  
o knows that a gathering has become unlawful and intentionally joins or  
stays in it, they are considered a member of an unlawful assembly. Such  
24  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
a member shall be punished with imprisonment for up to six months  
or with fine, or with both.  
o joins or remains in an unlawful assembly despite knowing that it has been  
lawfully ordered to disperse, they shall be punished with imprisonment  
for up to two years or with fine, or with both.  
o armed with a deadly weapon or anything likely to cause death, is part of  
an unlawful assembly, they shall be punished with imprisonment for up  
to two years or with fine, or with both.  
o knowingly stays in an assembly of five or more persons that is likely to  
cause a disturbance of public peace after being lawfully commanded to  
disperse, they shall be punished with imprisonment for up to six  
months or with fine, or with both.  
If the assembly is unlawful, the offender will be punished  
accordingly.  

Anyone who:  
hires, engages, employs, promotes, or knowingly supports the hiring of a  
o
person to join an unlawful assembly shall be punished as a member of  
that unlawful assembly. The person will be held accountable for any  
offenses committed by the hired individual as a member of the unlawful  
assembly, as if the person themselves were a member or had committed  
those offenses.  
o knowingly shelters, receives, or gathers people in their house or premises,  
being aware that these individuals have been hired, engaged, or  
employed, or are about to be hired, engaged, or employed to join or  
become members of an unlawful assembly, shall be punished with  
imprisonment for up to six months, or with a fine, or with both.  
o is hired, engaged, or attempts to be hired or engaged to do or assist in  
doing any of the acts as specified in the first provision of this section shall  
be punished with imprisonment for up to six months, or with a fine,  
or with both.  
anyone who while engaged or hired as referred to above, goes  
armed or engages in or offers to go armed with any deadly weapon  
or anything likely to cause death as a weapon of offense shall be  
punished with imprisonment for up to two years, or with a fine,  
or with both.  
.
.
EVERY MEMBER OF UNLAWFUL ASSEMBLY GUILTY OF OFFENCE COMMITTED  
IN PROSECUTION OF COMMON OBJECT (Section 190):  

If a crime is committed by any member of an unlawful assembly as part of  
the common goal of the assembly, or something that the members knew was  
likely to happen in pursuit of that goal, every person who is a member of the  
same assembly at the time of the offense is also guilty of that offense.  
RIOTING (Section 191):  
25  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  

When an unlawful assembly, or any member of it, uses force or violence in  
pursuit of their common objective, every member of that assembly is guilty of  
the offense of rioting.  


Punishment: imprisonment up to two years, or with fine, or with both.  
If someone participates in a riot while carrying a deadly weapon or anything that  
can be used to cause harm, they shall be punished with imprisonment up to  
five years or with fine, or with both.  
.
WANTONLY GIVING PROVOCATION WITH INTENT TO CAUSE RIOT-IF RIOTING BE  
COMMITTED; IF NOT COMMITTED (Section 192):  

If someone intentionally provokes another person, knowing it might lead to a riot,  
they shall be punished with imprisonment up to one year or with fine, or with  
both, if the riot occurs.  
o If the riot does not happen, the punishment shall be up to six months  
imprisonment or with fine, or with both.  
.
LIABILITY OF OWNER, OCCUPIER, ETC., OF LAND ON WHICH AN UNLAWFUL  
ASSEMBLY OR RIOT TAKES PLACE (Section 193):  



If there is an unlawful assembly or riot on someone's land, the owner or occupier  
must inform the nearest police station promptly and take lawful measures to  
prevent or stop it. Failure to do so, with knowledge or belief of the offense, shall  
be punishable with fine not exceeding one thousand rupees.  
If a riot benefits or is on behalf of a person linked to certain land or a dispute, that  
person shall be fined if they or their representatives, aware of the likelihood  
of the riot, do not take lawful measures to prevent it or disperse the unlawful  
assembly.  
If a riot occurs for the benefit of a person related to the land or a dispute, that  
person shall be fined if they or their representatives don't take lawful  
measures to prevent the riot or disperse the unlawful assembly, knowing it  
was likely to happen.  
.
.
AFFRAY (Section 194):  

If two or more people fight in a public place, causing a disturbance to public  
peace, it is referred to as committing an affray.  
Punishment: imprisonment for up to one month or with fine of up to one thousand  
rupees or with both.  

ASSAULTING OR OBSTRUCTING PUBLIC SERVANT WHEN SUPPRESSING RIOT,  
ETC. (Section 195):  

If anyone attacks or obstructs a public servant while they are performing their duty  
to disperse an unlawful assembly, suppress a riot, or handle an affray, they shall  
be punished with imprisonment up to three years, or with fine of not less  
than twenty-five thousand rupees, or with both.  
26  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  

If someone threatens or tries to obstruct a public servant, or uses force against  
them while they're doing their duty to disperse an unlawful assembly, suppress a  
riot, or handle an affray, they shall be punished with imprisonment for up to  
one year, or with fine, or with both.  
.
Promoting enmity between different groups on grounds of religion, race, place of  
birth, residence, language, etc., and doing acts prejudicial to maintenance of  
harmony (Section 196):  

Anyone:  
o promoting disharmony or fostering feelings of enmity, hatred, or ill-will  
between different religious, racial, language, or regional groups through  
words, signs, visible representations, electronic communication, or other  
means can be held accountable; or  
o engaging in actions that harm the harmony between different religious,  
racial, language, or regional groups, causing or likely to cause a  
disturbance to public tranquility, is prohibited; or  
o organizing or participating in activities with the intent to train participants to  
use criminal force or violence against any religious, racial, language, or  
regional group, causing fear or insecurity among its members, is prohibited.  
shall be punished with imprisonment up to three years, or with fine, or with both.  

Committing the offense specified above in a place of worship or during religious  
ceremonies shall be punishable with imprisonment up to five years and shall  
also be liable to fine.  
.
IMPUTATIONS, ASSERTIONS PREJUDICIAL TO NATIONAL INTEGRATION (Section  
197):  

Anyone by using spoken or written words, signs, visible representations,  
electronic communication, or any other means:  
o makes statements that suggest a group of people cannot, due to their  
identity, pledge allegiance to the Constitution or uphold India's sovereignty  
and integrity is not allowed; or  
o advocates or spreads the idea that any group of people, based on their  
religious, racial, language, or regional identity, should be denied or  
deprived of their rights as Indian citizens is prohibited; or  
o makes or publishes statements, pleas, or appeals that, based on identity,  
create disharmony or foster feelings of enmity, hatred, or ill-will between a  
group and others is not allowed; or  
o makes or publishes false or misleading information, jeopardising the  
sovereignty, unity and integrity or security of India  
shall be punished with imprisonment up to three years, or with fine, or with both.  

Committing the offences specified above in a place of worship or during religious  
ceremonies shall be punished with imprisonment for up to five years and shall  
also be liable for fine.
